clue.text: Cooked last of three dishes perhaps lacking third of meat?

definitions.text: Cooked last of three dishes perhaps lacking third of meat?

indicators.note: cooked food is worked over and changed, so the gathered letters are rearranged
last of picks only the final letter of three
lacking says the letter that follows is taken out of perhaps
third of picks the third letter of meat

explanation.surface: A puzzled cook wonders whether a third dish is missing some of its meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix E (end of 'three'), DISHES and PERHPS (PERHAPS without A, the third letter of 'meat'). The whole clue also describes the answer: a cooked dish whose meat may be scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's pie is a baked dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato, and the clue reads as a description of a batch of them.

clue.text: Could it be confusing to an Irish student of old?

indicators.note: confusing the words jumbles their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a puzzle might baffle a person from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A historian is a scholar who studies the past, which is what a student of old times does.

clue.text: Feet heard to stop for a while

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken and we take what it sounds like

parts.note: an animal's feet are its paws

explanation.surface: Someone hears footsteps halt for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to halt briefly before carrying on, a temporary cessation.

clue.text: Employ pundit, regardless of pressure

indicators.note: regardless of means paying no heed to, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a pundit is an expert
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A boss hires a commentator no matter how stressful the job is.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert strength or influence is to bring it into use, so to employ it.

clue.text: Edit clue, first of four condemned as underhand

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order
first of picks the opening letter of four

explanation.surface: An editor rejects a clue, one of four, as unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means sly and dishonest, which is what deceitful behaviour is.

clue.text: Views from master with time to go into particulars

parts.note: a master of a skill is a pro

indicators.note: to go into says the time letter is put inside the particulars

parts.note: specs are specifications, the particulars of something

explanation.surface: Opinions from an expert who will take time to examine the details.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospects are outlooks or vistas, so the word can mean views, as from a high place.

clue.text: Moved cautiously and led on, scratching head

indicators.note: scratching the head strikes out the first letter

parts.note: to tease someone is to lead them on

explanation.surface: Someone crept forward warily and strung someone along, perhaps scratching their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to move it slowly and carefully, as when easing a car into a space.

clue.text: Oppose return to university: student on vacation

parts.note: in British usage you come up to university, so returning is coming up again

indicators.note: vacation empties the word, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A student on holiday is set against going back to college.
explanation.walkthrough: Going up (or coming up) to Oxford or Cambridge is the British phrase for starting term; 'vacation' is also the university holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up against something is to meet it as an obstacle, so to oppose or confront it.

clue.text: Majority think again briefly when cutting caper

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so the shortened word sits within the caper

parts.note: to caper is to prance about

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to reponder is to ponder again

explanation.surface: Most people reconsider for a moment while leaping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caper' reads as a noun, a jape, but here it is the verb for leaping about.
explanation.definitionFit: A preponderance is the greater part or larger number, so a majority.

clue.text: Little-known degree held by Guardian's head of entertainment

indicators.note: held by means the degree sits inside the other word

parts.note: the setter writes for the Guardian, so the paper's own is ours
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of entertainment

explanation.surface: A degree held by the Guardian's head of entertainment is not widely known.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means not famous, known to few people.

clue.text: Snappier person coming over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more irritable, more cross
second meaning: one who crosses, as a road or the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The same word is a comparative adjective and an agent noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosser is both the comparative of cross, meaning angry, and someone who makes a crossing.

clue.text: Call up first wife, having received go-ahead

indicators.note: having received means taking something inside

parts.note: Eve was Adam's wife, the first in the Bible
OK means approval, the go-ahead

explanation.surface: Someone telephones his first wife once she has given approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or spirit is to summon it to mind, to call it up.

clue.text: Left in pieces after contestant finally made a mistake

indicators.note: after says the torn-up piece follows that letter
finally picks the closing letter of contestant

parts.note: paper left in pieces has been ripped up

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant who slipped up is left shattered.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip up is to stumble or blunder, so to make an error.

clue.text: Smarten up pages around margin

indicators.note: around says the pages enclose the margin

parts.note: a rim is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: An editor tidies pages by adjusting their margins.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom oneself fussily, making oneself neat and smart.

clue.text: Earth's level area included in test

parts.note: a plane is a flat, level surface

indicators.note: included in means the area letter goes inside the test

parts.note: to try is to test

explanation.surface: A flat region of the earth is measured as part of an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: Earth's is the possessive, an adjective-like sense, matching an adjective answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetary means belonging to a planet, so Earth's things are planetary ones.

clue.text: Thought to have left out light meal

indicators.note: out says the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: reflection is careful thought

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they skipped a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Refection is an old word for refreshment by food, especially a light repast.

clue.text: Imagined country united after one king, then another, beheaded queen

indicators.note: after says the united letter follows the first king

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king
another king, so another R

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Titania is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A fictional realm unites under kings in turn, then a queen loses her head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the made-up European kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Frantic Yale fugitive not fit, sadly, for such a place

indicators.note: frantic means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder
not says these letters are excluded from the pool
sadly says the excluded letters are scattered, not in a row

explanation.surface: A runaway from Yale, unwell and frantic, is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F, I and T from the letters of YALE FUGITIVE and rearrange the rest. Yale itself is the place the definition points back to.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of elite north-eastern American universities, of which Yale is a member.

clue.text: NB regular treatment needed for part of arm

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Note well: regular therapy is required for an injured limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb but means a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun barrel is the tube of a firearm, a weapon being an arm.

clue.text: Delayed training in troublesome communications app

indicators.note: delayed means put back later, so these letters go to the end

parts.note: pesky means annoying, troublesome
PE is physical education, physical training

explanation.surface: A buggy app holds up online training sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Skype is a well-known internet service for video and voice calls.

clue.text: Transport official parking in trendy part of town

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: in says the parking letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sector is a district or zone
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A traffic warden watches parking in a fashionable district.
explanation.definitionFit: On British buses and trains an inspector checks tickets, an official of public transport.

clue.text: Fibre's length unchanged on rotation

indicators.note: on rotation means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: as is means unchanged, in its present state

explanation.surface: A fibre keeps its length when spun.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Fibre's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Bound work with scarlet cover

indicators.note: cover means the scarlet wraps around the work

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A book is bound with a red jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Roped means tied up with rope, so bound.

clue.text: Father certainly repelled love goddess

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: aye means yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A priest firmly rejected a goddess of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility.

clue.text: Large leaf taken from soil often flipped over

indicators.note: flipped over says the hidden letters are read backwards
taken from says the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big leaf is lifted out of the earth and turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'taken' in the definition, but a folio is not 'taken'; 'taken from' is the signal that the letters sit inside 'soil often'.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet of paper folded once, a large page or leaf of a book.

clue.text: Suffer to keep up

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to maintain or keep going

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustain means both to undergo something bad, like damage, and to keep something going over time.

clue.text: Receding storm in film of the open seas

indicators.note: in says the reversed storm sits inside the film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a gale is a storm wind

explanation.surface: A movie shows a storm dying away at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelagic describes the deep ocean away from the coast, as in pelagic fish.

clue.text: Feign reluctance to give reason for theatre closure?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pretend not to be interested
second, whimsical meaning: say a show shut because it was difficult to get into

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a play that is hard to get to has an excuse for closing.
explanation.definitionFit: To play hard to get is an idiom for acting coy, and literally a play hard to get to would lose audiences.
